answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent must lock a stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so a spiral of fake accounts multiplies the cost for attackers instead of their reward. Reputation then accrues only through attested work, and the zenith of trust is reached gradually, never bought in bulk. A gale of fresh identities still arrives, but without stake and history they cannot vote, attest, or claim rewards, so Sybil farming stays unprofitable.
